newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China plans to issue 3.5 bln yuan railway bonds.
newsitem.headline: China plans to issue 3.5 bln yuan railway bonds.

text.p: China's Ministry of Railways plans to make a public offer of 3.5 billion yuan in railway bonds, an official of the ministry said on Wednesday.
The official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin that the offer required approvals from the State Planning Commission and the People's Bank of China.

The ministry expects to gain the approvals and launch the offer in the near future. It aims to use the proceeds to build facilities along China's 12 main railways, including the recently completed Beijing-Kowloon railway, he said.

The official said the ministry last year offered three-year railway construction bonds worth 1.53 billion yuan, with an annual interest rate of 15 percent. China Securities Co Ltd as the chief underwriter, he said.
